results.summary: A cohesive Kafka-like streaming design with partitioned durable storage, explicit leader fencing, replayable consumer offsets, and a clear at-least-once processing path.

findings.title: Partitioned log architecture aligns with core streaming requirements
findings.explanation: The broker is modeled as an append-only commit log with partition-level ordering, replication, replay retention, and consumer-group offsets. This covers publish/subscribe, durability, replay, and horizontal scale coherently.

findings.title: Failure-domain fencing is explicitly handled in the control plane
findings.explanation: The coordination service fences stale leaders and restricts leader election to the authoritative quorum during partitions, which directly supports safe failover and avoids split-brain writes.

findings.title: At-least-once processing path is clearly specified
findings.explanation: The processing path uses stable event IDs, idempotent effects, and checkpoint-after-effect semantics, which makes the default consumer behavior concrete and compatible with replay and retries.

findings.title: Scalable partition fan-out supports throughput goals
findings.explanation: Partitioned routing, independent consumer groups, and a separate real-time processing engine provide a workable strategy for high throughput without demanding global ordering.

results.summary: Strong autocomplete architecture with localized prefix retrieval, caching, ranking, and async projection; the main gaps are explicit freshness handling during update lag and clearer candidate merge rules for the top-N response path.

findings.title: Real-time update freshness is only eventual
findings.explanation: Catalog and interaction updates are propagated asynchronously through the event stream and projection workers, but the read path does not define a freshness threshold, synchronous fallback, or stale-data policy. That makes the requirement to update suggestions in real time only partially supported because the design depends on projection lag staying low rather than enforcing a freshness guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit freshness policy such as bounded staleness, a recent-update bypass, or a version check that routes around stale cache/index state when updates are pending.

findings.title: Projection lag can delay real-time freshness
findings.explanation: Catalog and interaction updates are propagated asynchronously through the event stream and projection workers, and the design exposes lag metrics, but the read path does not define a freshness threshold, synchronous fallback, or stale-data policy for periods when the index/cache has not yet caught up. That leaves real-time suggestion updates dependent on backlog conditions rather than an explicit freshness guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Define the freshness behavior for reads during update lag, such as a bounded staleness window, a fallback to the canonical catalog for hot changes, or a read-time version check that bypasses stale cache entries.

findings.title: Candidate merge and de-duplication policy is implicit
findings.explanation: The read API fetches candidates from cache, prefix index, and user-history-informed ranking, but the submission does not state how overlapping suggestions are deduplicated or which source wins when cached, indexed, and personalized signals disagree. That makes the exact top-N assembly path ambiguous.
findings.recommendation: Specify the merge order and de-duplication rules before ranking, including source precedence and tie-breaking when the same term arrives from multiple candidate sources.

results.summary: The design credibly covers distributed key-value CRUD, configurable consistency, horizontal scaling, durable replication, automatic failure handling, and bounded range queries with an explicitly managed freshness trade-off.

findings.title: Asynchronous range index is an intentional freshness trade-off
findings.explanation: The range index is explicitly derived and may lag the committed base change stream, but the coordinator compensates by fetching current base values and surfacing freshness metadata. This is a coherent design choice for supporting range queries without making the index authoritative.

findings.title: Consistency is exposed as an operation-level choice
findings.explanation: The client, gateway, coordinator, and replica interaction all carry the requested consistency level, which makes availability-versus-consistency behavior explicit instead of implicit.

findings.title: Repair and observability are integrated into the core paths
findings.explanation: Membership, repair, projection lag, and quorum shortfalls are tracked through dedicated monitoring and maintenance flows, which supports operating a partitioned distributed database.

results.summary: The design is a coherent distributed crawler with host-sharded frontier management, robots-aware politeness, duplicate suppression, JS rendering, and durable storage suitable for billion-scale crawling.

findings.title: Strong billion-scale frontier design
findings.explanation: The combination of canonicalization, host sharding, durable frontier state, and lease-based dispatch is well matched to billion-URL crawling without keeping the whole crawl set in memory.

findings.title: Robots and politeness are handled end-to-end
findings.explanation: Robots.txt is evaluated separately from host authorization, and the shared politeness gate prevents accidental permission escalation while respecting crawl-delay and Retry-After signals.

findings.title: Efficient duplicate suppression strategy
findings.explanation: The design pairs Bloom hints with exact registry checks and content digests, which limits expensive exact lookups while keeping duplicate decisions safe.

results.summary: The design covers uploads, social graph, interactions, feed, stories, search, messaging, and the stated scale/latency/availability constraints with coherent service boundaries and data flows.

findings.title: Hybrid feed strategy addresses celebrity-scale fanout
findings.explanation: The feed service distinguishes ordinary authors from celebrity authors and uses fan-out-on-write for the common path plus fan-out-on-read for high-fanout accounts, which is a strong fit for the published scale constraint.

findings.title: Direct media upload avoids routing large bodies through application servers
findings.explanation: The client uploads directly to the media object store with scoped authorization, which is a good implementation choice for high-availability uploads and media efficiency.

findings.title: Dedicated story expiry handling prevents correctness from depending on TTL timing
findings.explanation: The stories service enforces expiry at read time and uses TTL cleanup only for reclamation, which is robust against delayed background deletion.

results.summary: The design covers paste creation, short unique URLs, aliases, expiry, client-side highlighting, view counting, and large-text handling with a coherent low-latency read path and asynchronous maintenance.

findings.title: Clear read-path separation from analytics and cleanup
findings.explanation: The architecture keeps paste retrieval independent from view aggregation and expiry cleanup, which is well matched to a read-heavy paste service with low-latency goals.

findings.title: Consistent handling of short unique identifiers and aliases
findings.explanation: Key generation, conditional reservation, and alias conflict handling are aligned so generated URLs remain short and collision-safe without a central counter.

findings.title: Asynchronous view counting preserves retrieval latency
findings.explanation: The design records successful GETs through a queue and worker path, allowing counts to remain eventually consistent while avoiding a write on every read.

results.summary: The design covers real-time autocomplete with top-N ranking, typo tolerance, personalization, locale handling, and async updates using a coherent read/write split and scalable prefix infrastructure.

findings.title: Stateless read path and cache/index split support scale
findings.explanation: The submission cleanly separates hot read serving from async writes, uses a cache for popular prefixes, and keeps the read API stateless for horizontal scaling. That is a strong fit for the stated query volume.

findings.title: Locale-aware partial-query flow is well articulated
findings.explanation: Locale is preserved from client to gateway to read orchestration, and the prefix index is explicitly locale-aware. This supports both language-sensitive ranking and partial-query matching.

findings.title: Asynchronous update pipeline preserves freshness without blocking reads
findings.explanation: Catalog changes are committed before event publication, then replayed into index and cache updates by idempotent workers. This is a solid pattern for real-time suggestion freshness.

results.summary: The design is strong and mostly complete, with robust metadata/object separation, conflict-aware sync, and secure sharing; the main gap is that content search is only explicit for supported file formats rather than all stored files.

findings.title: Content search is limited to supported formats
findings.explanation: The design clearly supports name search and content extraction for explicitly supported formats, but it does not claim full content search for every stored file type. That makes the core search capability only partially satisfied if the expectation is that all files are searchable by content.
findings.recommendation: Clarify the expected search scope, or add broader extraction/indexing coverage and a fallback strategy for unsupported file types if universal content search is required.

results.summary: The design covers multi-channel notifications, preference handling, templates, delivery tracking, rate limiting, retries, analytics, A/B testing, and high-scale delivery with a coherent event-driven architecture.

findings.title: Channel-aware orchestration and isolated delivery paths
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates command ingestion, policy evaluation, outbox publication, and channel-specific delivery workers/queues. This reduces coupling and makes it easier to apply per-channel quotas and retries without impacting other channels.

findings.title: Privacy-preserving data handling is consistently reflected in storage and analytics
findings.explanation: Sensitive values are encrypted, authorization is enforced around preference/inbox data, and downstream analytics excludes raw addresses, device tokens, IPs, and message bodies. That is a strong match for the privacy constraint.

findings.title: End-to-end delivery state is modeled beyond simple sent/not-sent status
findings.explanation: The orchestrator, event stream, and provider callbacks represent accepted, attempted, delivered, bounced, suppressed, failed, and delayed states with timestamps. That gives a concrete basis for delivery tracking and reconciliation.

results.summary: A coherent distributed metrics pipeline is defined from host agents through durable streaming, real-time aggregation, hot querying, archival storage, alerting, and dashboards, with clear handling for metric types, bursts, and historical access.

findings.title: Typed metrics are preserved through ingestion and aggregation
findings.explanation: Counters, gauges, and histograms are handled with type-specific semantics instead of being flattened into a generic sample stream, which preserves reset handling and histogram compatibility.

findings.title: Burst handling uses both admission control and durable replay
findings.explanation: The ingestion path combines client-aware admission control with a durable stream and bounded backpressure, which is a coherent strategy for bursty write traffic.

findings.title: Historical access is separated from hot-query serving
findings.explanation: Recent reads go to the time-series hot store while older data is routed to the archive, which supports low-latency operational queries without forcing all history into the hot tier.

results.summary: A coherent distributed rate-limiting architecture centered on a policy-driven gateway with atomic Redis state, versioned policy refresh, and off-path telemetry; it supports multiple algorithms, tiered limits, and actionable 429 responses.

findings.title: Default token bucket plus policy-selected alternatives is a strong fit for the scope
findings.explanation: The submitted design cleanly separates algorithm choice from enforcement: token bucket is the default, while fixed-window, sliding-window, and leaky-bucket remain available when a policy’s burst, precision, memory, or smoothing tradeoff makes them preferable. This directly supports multi-algorithm requirements without complicating the request path.

findings.title: Asynchronous telemetry keeps breach monitoring off the hot path
findings.explanation: Breach and health signals are sent to a queue and aggregated before reaching monitoring, so alerting does not add synchronous latency to request admission. This is a good match for a high-throughput limiter.

results.summary: A coherent Kafka-like streaming architecture with partitioned logs, quorum-fenced leadership, durable offsets, replayable consumption, and real-time processing; it covers the stated core scope and constraints well.

findings.title: Partition-aware ordering and replay are consistently modeled
findings.explanation: The design keeps order within a partition, preserves committed offsets per consumer group, and routes keyed records to the same partition, which matches the required ordering and replay semantics without inventing a global total order.

findings.title: Failure handling uses fencing and commit-after-replication correctly
findings.explanation: Leadership fencing in the coordination service and acknowledgement only after the in-sync replica commit policy reduce the chance of divergent logs and acknowledged loss during replica or leader failures.

findings.title: Operational visibility covers the main stream health signals
findings.explanation: Monitoring captures append latency, throughput, skew, replication health, coordinator elections, consumer lag, retries, dead-letter counts, and checkpoint age, which is sufficient for this exercise’s core operational visibility needs.

results.summary: The design cleanly covers CRUD, configurable consistency, hash-based scale-out, durable storage, automatic failure handling, and bounded range queries with a coherent coordinator/index/repair split.

findings.title: Partition-aware consistency and failure handling are end-to-end
findings.explanation: The submitted architecture propagates requested consistency from client to gateway to coordinator, uses replica ownership from a versioned token map, and returns explicit conflict/unavailable/unknown-outcome states when replicas cannot satisfy the request. That is a coherent fit for the core availability and consistency scope.

findings.title: Range access is separated from point-key storage in a sensible way
findings.explanation: The design keeps hash-partitioned primary storage for point operations and uses an ordered secondary index for bounded scans, with base-store fetches for current values. This preserves the point-lookup scale strategy while still supporting range queries.

findings.title: Durability path is well articulated
findings.explanation: Committed mutations flow into a durable change log, the primary store advertises durable acknowledgments, and the design includes backups and point-in-time recovery. This gives a clear persistence story for both writes and repair.

results.summary: The design covers the crawler’s core scope with durable host-sharded scheduling, layered canonicalization and deduplication, robots/politeness enforcement, selective JavaScript rendering, and efficient snapshot storage.

findings.title: Host-politeness and robots enforcement are centralized before fetch/render
findings.explanation: The design keeps permission to fetch separate from scheduling, and both static and browser-rendered work must pass the shared host politeness gate after robots evaluation. This directly supports crawler correctness under per-site limits.

findings.title: Canonical registry and Bloom hints provide layered duplicate control
findings.explanation: URL canonicalization, exact registry checks, and Bloom membership hints are combined so duplicates are filtered efficiently while exact confirmation remains durable in the registry.

findings.title: Separated static and JavaScript fetch paths preserve scale
findings.explanation: Most pages can flow through the polite static fetch fleet, while only eligible pages are routed to the JS render pool. That separation keeps expensive browser work from consuming the entire crawl budget.

results.summary: The design covers paste creation, short unique URLs, aliases, expiry, syntax highlighting, view counting, and high-volume read-optimized retrieval with a coherent CDN/cache/object-store/work queue split.

findings.title: Asynchronous view counting preserves read-path performance
findings.explanation: Successful GETs are emitted from the edge into a durable queue and aggregated by background workers, so view tracking does not add a write to each retrieval and still includes cache hits.

findings.title: Expiration is enforced before cleanup completes
findings.explanation: The metadata layer rejects reads at expiry, then workers tombstone and retry object deletion idempotently. This prevents delayed cleanup from extending the lifetime of an expired paste.

findings.title: Short-code generation avoids centralized counters
findings.explanation: The key generator produces compact random base36 candidates while the metadata store remains the uniqueness authority, which is a good fit for concurrent short URL creation.

results.summary: The design provides a coherent low-latency autocomplete pipeline with stateless reads, hot-prefix caching, distributed prefix lookup, relevance ranking, personalization, and asynchronous index updates.

findings.title: Hybrid read path balances freshness and latency
findings.explanation: The design combines a hot-prefix cache, a distributed prefix index, and a separate ranking service, which is a strong fit for a high-read autocomplete workload while keeping the request handler stateless.

findings.title: Locale-aware flow is threaded through the main read path
findings.explanation: Locale is carried from the client through the gateway into cache, index, and ranking components, so the design has a coherent basis for multilingual suggestion behavior.

results.summary: The design covers the core file storage, sharing, versioning, sync, search, large-file transfer, offline access, scale, durability, and conflict-handling requirements with coherent service boundaries and direct transfer paths.

findings.title: Server-side conflict preservation is well defined
findings.explanation: The design explicitly avoids silent last-writer-wins behavior by comparing each write against its base revision and retaining the losing edit as a conflict version. This directly supports concurrent edits and offline reconciliation.

findings.title: Hybrid feed distribution strategy is well matched to celebrity scale
findings.explanation: The feed service combines fan-out-on-write for ordinary authors with fan-out-on-read for celebrity authors, which is a strong fit for the stated need to handle accounts with millions of followers while preserving low-latency reads for typical users.

findings.title: Direct media upload path avoids routing large blobs through application servers
findings.explanation: The client uploads media directly to object storage, and the processing worker consumes completed upload work asynchronously. This preserves API capacity and supports the upload availability constraint.

findings.title: Story expiry is enforced in the service, not only by cleanup
findings.explanation: The stories service checks expiry on every read while the metadata store uses TTL cleanup for reclamation. That avoids correctness depending on delayed background deletion.

findings.title: Search is modeled as derived data with visibility filtering
findings.explanation: User and hashtag search is implemented as a derived index updated from profile and post services, with visibility filtering in the gateway/search path. This is appropriate for keeping search responsive while respecting current privacy state.

results.summary: The design cleanly places rate limiting at the gateway with shared Redis state, versioned tier policies, async telemetry, and explicit support for multiple algorithms, covering the published core scope well.

findings.title: Token bucket default with per-policy algorithm selection
findings.explanation: The gateway chooses token bucket as the default algorithm while preserving fixed-window, sliding-window, and leaky-bucket options by policy version. This cleanly satisfies the multi-algorithm constraint without coupling all tenants to one policy shape.

findings.title: Shared Redis state for distributed correctness
findings.explanation: Using an authoritative Redis shard with atomic check-and-update gives a strong distributed coordination story for rate-limit correctness and reset semantics.

findings.title: Clear client-facing 429 response path
findings.explanation: The gateway returns a stable 429 error plus rate-limit headers and retry guidance, which is exactly the kind of user-visible failure behavior the brief asks for.

results.summary: The design provides a coherent multi-channel notification platform with durable fanout, per-channel isolation, preference enforcement, template/version management, retries, analytics, and spike-friendly scaling.

findings.title: End-to-end multi-channel delivery flow is well decomposed
findings.explanation: The submission cleanly separates command intake, policy/orchestration, outbox dispatch, per-channel queues, delivery workers, and provider adapters. This makes the required multi-channel behavior implementable without tight coupling to vendors.

findings.title: Privacy-sensitive data handling is consistently applied
findings.explanation: Opaque recipient/device references, encrypted registries, redacted analytics, and avoidance of raw address storage in the ledger reduce exposure across operational and analytical paths.

findings.title: No material core defect demonstrated from the submitted architecture
findings.explanation: The design covers the published core scope with coherent control-plane and data-plane separation, retry handling, analytics, rate limiting, and traffic-spike scaling. No required behavior is left unsupported by the evidence provided.

results.summary: A coherent distributed metrics pipeline is defined end to end: agents ingest typed metrics through an authenticated gateway, a durable stream absorbs bursts, real-time aggregation feeds hot and historical storage, and queries, dashboards, and threshold alerts are supported.

findings.title: Type-aware metric handling is preserved across the pipeline
findings.explanation: Counters, gauges, and histograms are not flattened into a single generic sample model; the ingestion, aggregation, query, and dashboard layers keep type-specific semantics visible. This is a strong fit for correct rate, trend, and distribution analysis.

findings.title: Tiered storage and rollup-aware querying support both recent and historical access
findings.explanation: The hot store serves recent range queries while the archive keeps compressed historical blocks, allowing the query service to choose between raw and rolled-up data based on range and dimension filters.

findings.title: scores are not lower because the design includes explicit burst absorption
findings.explanation: The gateway, broker, and producer backpressure path show a coherent strategy for sustained spikes without unbounded ingestion growth.

results.summary: A Kafka-like stream platform with partitioned append-only storage, leader fencing, replayable consumer offsets, real-time processing, and monitoring for latency, lag, and replication health.

findings.title: Partition-level ordering with replay preserves the required stream semantics
findings.explanation: The design keeps ordering local to partitions, routes stable keys consistently, and exposes durable offsets for replay. That combination matches the brief while preserving horizontal parallelism.

findings.title: Replication-acknowledgement path is aligned with durability and failure handling
findings.explanation: Acknowledging writes only after the configured in-sync replica policy is met, together with fencing stale leaders, directly supports no-loss recovery behavior under broker failures and network partitions.

findings.title: Operational metrics are scoped to the stream-specific recovery and scaling signals
findings.explanation: The monitoring service tracks append latency, throughput, partition skew, replication health, controller elections, consumer lag, retries, and checkpoint age, which is enough to reason about load, backlog, and recovery.

results.summary: A cohesive distributed KV-store design with partition-aware routing, quorum consistency, durable base storage, asynchronous range indexing, and explicit repair/monitoring paths aligned to the published scope.

findings.title: Consistent partition-aware routing and repair loop
findings.explanation: The design cleanly separates request routing, membership dissemination, durable base storage, asynchronous index projection, and replica repair. That gives a coherent path for node churn and bounded range access without overloading the primary write path.

findings.title: Explicit consistency choices are exposed end to end
findings.explanation: The client, gateway, and coordinator all carry the requested consistency level and return explicit conflict/unavailable/unknown-outcome states, which makes the trade-off visible rather than implicit.

findings.title: Durability strategy is layered
findings.explanation: The primary store uses durable logs, backups, and PITR, while the change log provides replayable mutation events for projection and repair. That improves recovery posture without tying correctness to one mechanism.

results.summary: The design cleanly covers billion-scale distributed crawling, including robots enforcement, deduplication, dynamic content rendering, trap avoidance, durable frontiering, and efficient storage.

findings.title: Host-sharded crawl path is well decomposed
findings.explanation: The design separates discovery, canonicalization, shard routing, frontier persistence, host politeness gating, fetching, rendering, parsing, and durable storage into clear stages. This supports large-scale crawling while keeping responsibilities legible.

findings.title: Robots and rate limiting are enforced before fetch and render
findings.explanation: The robots evaluator, policy cache, and shared host gate are wired so that policy decisions and per-host delays are checked before requests are dispatched. That is a strong fit for crawl politeness and repeatable policy enforcement.
